message.content: hey bestie, take a look at src/zodiacPositions.ts, particularly from line 292 onwards. This is a sort of god object for the project that I accidentally created. To my own credit it's not that bad, it is relatively narrow in its behaviour/purpose domain: all it does is know where stuff is. It understands extremely little about astrology, 90% of its job is just to know the ecliptic longitude of a bunch of things we care about, and it can also answer some cursory questions about what's the sign/house/orientation of this node (so it understands that some of its positions define ranges, but nothing else). Nonetheless, I am growing gradually more irritated with it - from lines 308-311 you can gleam that it tracks the positions of four very-much-not-the-same-kind-of-objects: astrological nodes, house cusps, zodiac sign starting points, and fixed stars. I would thus want to split this class into four, in a way that's very canonical because it's private attributes literally tell you what these classes should be called: NodePositions, HouseCuspPositions, ZodiacSymbolPositions, FixedStarPositions. However you can see that this task is a bit daunting, because the state logic within ZodiacPositions is not trivial - particularly this is owing mostly to the fact that it is an immutable object. Let me explain. It depends on a date, a location, and a series of configuration parameters. Any change to the date or location will force recomputation of everything (with some small exceptions, but eh). However, the configuration values may only affect small portions of the state. This is why the constructor actually allows you to directly pass all the internal state, and then we have the private copyWith method, that returns an exact copy of the current instance changing only the specified bits, and then you can do functions like changeLunarNodeMode at 407-415, which receives a new value for the configuration value LunarNodeMode, changes only what's relevant to this, and returns a copy of the whole object having changed only what's affected by the LunarNodeMode (as well as the LunarNodeMode itself, of course). This is then used in App.tsx liness 150-152 - instead of making zodiacPositions be an useMemo that recomputes the whole thing whenever lunarNodeMode changes, we just have this useEffect to handle that particular change and everything works beautifully. I came up with this myself, as it is my first time working with react, but from what I can tell this is a relatively standard pattern to have "mutability" in immutable objects that have some non-trivial dependencies on their inputs, thus avoiding unnecessary recomputation. Alright so, anyway, we'll want to split things up and probably have the same pattern for each of the four resulting objects. NodePositions depends entirely (i.e. no changeXYZ function, just recompute) on date and surfacePosition, and depends partially on lunarNodeMode and hamburgSchoolMode. Nothing else. HouseCuspPositions depends entirely on date, surfacePosition, and houseSystem, and partially on housePresweep (actually this.housePresweep sort of counts as internal state, it's just that this internal state is literally the exact same value as the configuration, so...). ZodiacSymbolPositions depends entirely on date and astrologyMode. I'm also noticing now that siderealOffset is part of the state and not the config (the logic is a bit funny, you'll see when you read the class) - again nothing wrong with this, that state can go to ZodiacSymbolPositions, it just confused me a bit just now how it not being private made me think it was a config value). And finally fixedStarPositions depends only on the date. So the simple act of splitting this class into four, conceptually, isn't that hard. We will presumably split it into four files, NodePositions will probably keep most of the helper functions in zodiacPositions.ts, the remainder will get split between the other three or possibly put somewhere else and exported, probably astronomyUtil.ts. Speaking of astronomyUtil.ts, it probably should also contain computeLunarApogeePerigeeMeeus, computeLunarApogeePerigeeExact, computeLunarNodesMeeus and computeLunarNodesExact - nobody else uses these functions but it makes sense that astronomy code goes in astronomyUtil.ts. HouseCuspPositions kind of already has its own file - house logic is so extensive it went to houses.ts. There are some complications with this one. Two, specifically. (1) the big dispatch function, computeHouseCuspPositions, actually takes an object analogous to NodePositions. This is solely to know where the main angles are for things like porphyry. We can just eliminate this dependency and compute the main angles locally when necessary, since we in fact already have to do this for other house systems that require the full position of these points - the relevant functions are already imported from geometry.ts, particularly computeAllSignificantPoints, and there's probably some other function already imported, or otherwise in astronomyUtil.ts, that will serve to go from full 3d position -> ecliptic longitude. We can do this internally in computeHouseCuspPositions and thus eschew the NodePositions dependency. The ZodiacSymbolPositions dependency is more relevant, and I actually just forgot about it earlier. Here we could eliminate the dependency and work directly off of AstrologyMode, but I think it is cleaner to just let ZodiacSymbolPositions be a dependency. As for the other two, FixedStarPositions should be very simple, and ZodiacSymbolPositions will end up a bit wonky but this wonkiness will be 100% inherited from zodiacPositions, particularly the whole handling regular/irregular zodiac systems within the same class. This will be a massive refactor, so there's a few other things we can take the time to do. First of all, standarize naming. Is it "Zodiac Symbol" or "Zodiac Sign"? The codebase is all over the place with this. We need to pick one and stick to it. Also, "Astrology Mode" is a pretty silly name too, it's leftover because it was the first config option and it seemed more relevant back then - probably "Zodiac mode" instead? But let me know if you have a better idea. Oh, and note the public function houseSystemUndefinedForPosition that zodiacPositions has - HouseCuspPositions will inherit this function. Maybe? Or maybe whatever function returns houseCuspPositions: HouseCuspPositions should also be allowed to return null in certain cases? This is closer to how things currently work, where ZodiacPositions._houseCuspPositions is allowed to be null. Yes, I think that makes more sense, let me know what you think. Also HouseCuspPositions will have a new method, areHouseCuspsWithinHouse, which will return true if housePresweep is false or if no houses are narrower than five degrees - you can see the point of this. And also we'll later add support for presweeps different from exactly 5 degrees, but don't worry about that, I'll do it myself, I'm just listing this all off because first of all I want you to help me with the to-do list. Okay, so that's all great, but so far we're only talking about internal stuff. How will the rest of the code handle this? I sort of view this through the simpler question of, e.g., "where will the method getHouseOfNode go live after this"? Will it go to astrologyUtil.ts, which is already basically just "ZodiacPositions methods that I didn't want to put in ZodiacPositions", and after the refactor it will be clear that it actually depends on NodePositions and HouseCuspPositions? Or will we create some new but slightly better segregated god object, call it AstrologicalChart, that has private state _nodePositions, _houseCuspPositions, etc... it's basically the same as ZodiacPositions, but better segregated, and because it has "Astrological" in the name I am now comfortable with putting all kinds of astrology in there, all the stuff that would ordinarily go in astrologyUtils.ts. I have many thoughts about this idea. First of all, my OOP brain is really into it. But it _is_ basically the same as the object I'm currently trying to get rid of, potentially plus a bunch of extra methods. It seems like a huge issue that if we want its internals to be private, we'll have to expose a bunch of changeXYZ functions too, essentially doubling all that code. This makes me confident that this is actually a bad idea. But maybe we actually let the internals be public, and then we can have exactly the same client code to handle updates, but instead of setZodiacPositions(zodiacPositions.changeLunarNodeMode(lunarNodeMode)), we'll have something like setAstrologicalChart(astrologicalChart.changeNodePositions(nodePositions.changeLunarNodeMode(lunarNodeMode)) - both of these would be an useEffect depending on lunarNodeMode. This would require exposing four changeXYZ (nodepositions, housecusp... etc), which is still not great but I think tolerable and not absurd. In this way AstrologicalChart is a much looser object, stuff can be slotted in/out whenever, and it basically just becomes a convenience wrapper to be able to call asstrologicalChart.getHouseOfNode(node) instead of getHouseOfNode(node, nodePositions, houseCuspPositions). I'm really not sure which is better: AstrologicalChart really just seems like it adds a bunch of boilerplate just to soothe the part of my brain that likes doing everything with OOP. I'm really not too sure. The "no AstrologicalChart" option seems like it will make my life easier when I later reutilize these objects to make e.g. transit charts, but really, only a little bit - the end result will not be that different. I'm not sure at all, in general. What do you think? Okay, so we've covered the internals of the refactor, the interface of the refactor with the client code, and, of course, we also have to refactor the client code: this will be a little bit complex in App.tsx as we dial in the specific updating logic, but apart from that we'll just have to walk through the code, switch out every instance of zodiacPositions as a prop with the specific dependencies (rarely all four of them)*, which involves a bit of thinking about what these dependencies are, and then just looking through every callsite and changing the names to the new names, which will be easy but very mindnumbing. Oh, and I realize now that the asterisk I just put down is probably the final nail in the coffin of the AstrologicalChart idea - bundling it all into one object causes react to see it as one immutable object (duh), so this very much has the potential to cause more rerenders than necessary by obscuring the specific dependencies - stuff that e.g. really just depends on the houseCuspPositions will now depend on "the whole astrological chart", and will thus... etc etc you know where this is going. Okay, that's all - and also after we're done and NodePositions is separated out, we'll use that to really easily create NodeVelocities, you can guess how - but again that's an "after we're done" thing. Okay, so your first task is actually to organize all this into a "refactor spec", so to speak, project plan, to-do list, however you like to call it. First of all let's dial down the details: Is there anything above that didn't entirely make sense to you, or any open question I left that we need to be specific about? Let's clear that up first by talking here, and once we're done I'll ask you to draft a refactor spec txt. Okay, let me know your thoughts.

input.content:
ZODIAC POSITIONS REFACTOR SPEC
===============================

Goal: Split the ZodiacPositions god object into four focused immutable classes,
each with its own copyWith/changeXYZ pattern, and update all call sites.

NAMING DECISIONS
----------------
- "Zodiac Symbol" -> "Zodiac Sign" (everywhere in the codebase)
- "AstrologyMode" -> "ZodiacMode" (everywhere: type, enum, settings, UI)
- "astrologyUtil.ts" -> "chartAnalysis.ts"
- The four new classes: NodePositions, HouseCuspPositions, ZodiacSignPositions, FixedStarPositions


PHASE 1: EXTRACT HELPER FUNCTIONS
----------------------------------
Move from zodiacPositions.ts to astronomyUtil.ts:
  - computeLunarApogeePerigeeMeeus
  - computeLunarApogeePerigeeExact
  - computeLunarNodesMeeus
  - computeLunarNodesExact
  (Plus their dispatchers computeLunarApogeePerigee, computeLunarNodes)

These are pure astronomy functions with no business being in zodiacPositions.ts.
They'll be imported by NodePositions.


PHASE 2: CREATE THE FOUR CLASSES
---------------------------------

Each class follows the same immutable-with-copyWith pattern as current ZodiacPositions.

2A. FixedStarPositions (new file: fixedStarPositions.ts)
  - Simplest of the four.
  - Depends entirely on: date
  - No changeXYZ methods needed (only date causes change, and date change = full recompute)
  - State: _positions: Map<string, number>
  - Public: getPositions(), getPosition(name)
  - Constructor takes date, optional precomputed positions.

2B. ZodiacSignPositions (new file: zodiacSignPositions.ts)
  - Depends entirely on: date, zodiacMode (renamed from astrologyMode)
  - No partial-recompute changeXYZ needed (both inputs cause full recompute)
    Wait - actually changeZodiacMode exists (was changeAstrologyMode). The date
    triggers full recompute, but zodiacMode can change independently, so:
  - changeZodiacMode(newMode): recomputes sign positions + siderealOffset only
  - State:
      _signPositions: Map<Zodiac, number>
      siderealOffset: number | null  (public, as before)
      date: Date
      zodiacMode: ZodiacMode
  - Public methods:
      getSignPositions()
      isRegular(): boolean  (was isZodiacModeRegular)
      getSignAtLongitude(lon): Zodiac  (was _getSymbolAtLongitude)
      getSignOfNode(lon): Zodiac  -- wait, this takes a Node, it needs NodePositions
        Actually: we refactor this. getSignAtLongitude(lon) is the primitive.
        getSignOfNode was a convenience that did getNodePosition then getSignAtLongitude.
        After the split, callers do: zodiacSignPositions.getSignAtLongitude(nodePositions.get(node))
        Or we keep a convenience as a free function in chartAnalysis.ts.
      getPositionWithinSign(lon): number  (takes raw longitude, not Node)

2C. HouseCuspPositions (new file: houseCuspPositions.ts)
  - Depends entirely on: date, surfacePosition, houseSystem, zodiacSignPositions
  - Depends partially on: housePresweep (trivial - stored config, no recomputation)
  - Can be null: when surfacePosition is null, or when house system is undefined
    for the given position/time (Placidus/Koch at extreme latitudes).
    So: the producing code returns HouseCuspPositions | null.
  - Eliminates dependency on NodePositions in computeHouseCuspPositions:
    Currently houses.ts:computeHouseCuspPositions takes knownNodes just to extract
    ASC/DSC/MC/IC. Instead, compute these internally from (date, surfacePosition)
    using computeAllSignificantPoints + getTodayEclipticLongitudeFromEQJ (move this
    helper to astronomyUtil.ts or keep in houses.ts as local).
    New signature: computeHouseCuspPositions(date, surfacePosition, houseSystem, zodiacSignPositions)
  - changeHouseSystem(newSystem, zodiacSignPositions): recomputes cusps
  - changeHousePresweep(newValue): copyWith, no recomputation
  - changeZodiacSignPositions(newZSP): recomputes only if houseSystem is
    ayanamsa-dependant (whole sign systems). Otherwise returns this.
  - State:
      _cuspPositions: number[]
      date, surfacePosition, houseSystem, housePresweep
  - Public methods:
      getCuspPositions(): number[]
      getCuspPosition(i): number
      getHouseOfNode(lon: number): number  (takes longitude, not Node)
        -- presweep logic stays here
      areHouseCuspsWithinHouse(): boolean
        -- returns true if housePresweep is false OR no house is narrower than 5 degrees

2D. NodePositions (new file: nodePositions.ts)
  - The beefiest one. Keeps most helper functions from current zodiacPositions.ts.
  - Depends entirely on: date, surfacePosition
  - Depends partially on: lunarNodeMode, hamburgSchoolMode
  - changeLunarNodeMode(newMode): recomputes lunar nodes + apogee/perigee only
  - changeHamburgSchoolMode(newMode): recomputes hamburg school objects only
  - State:
      _positions: Map<Node, number>
      date, surfacePosition, lunarNodeMode, hamburgSchoolMode
  - Public methods:
      getPositions(): Map<Node, number>
      get(node): number  (was getNodePosition)
      has(node): boolean
      hasSurfacePosition(): boolean
      isAboveHorizon(node): boolean  (was isNodeAboveHorizon)
      isEastern(node): boolean  (was isNodeEastern)
  - Contains/imports all the compute functions:
      computePhysicalNodePositions, computeSmallObjectPositions,
      computeHamburgSchoolObjectPositions, computeAxisAngles,

ZODIAC POSITIONS REFACTOR SPEC
===============================

Goal: Split the ZodiacPositions god object into four focused immutable classes,
each with its own copyWith/changeXYZ pattern, and update all call sites.

NAMING DECISIONS
----------------
- "Zodiac Symbol" -> "Zodiac Sign" (everywhere in the codebase)
- "AstrologyMode" -> "ZodiacMode" (everywhere: type, enum, settings, UI)
- "astrologyUtil.ts" -> "chartAnalysis.ts"
- The four new classes: NodePositions, HouseCuspPositions, ZodiacSignPositions, FixedStarPositions


PHASE 1: EXTRACT HELPER FUNCTIONS
----------------------------------
Move from zodiacPositions.ts to astronomyUtil.ts:
  - computeLunarApogeePerigeeMeeus
  - computeLunarApogeePerigeeExact
  - computeLunarNodesMeeus
  - computeLunarNodesExact
  (Plus their dispatchers computeLunarApogeePerigee, computeLunarNodes)
  USER NOTE: No, their dispatchers stay where they are. The notion of dispatching according to LunarNodeMode we do not consider to be astronomical, it belongs to the object that actually knows that the LunarNodeMode is, i.e. NodePositions.

These are pure astronomy functions with no business being in zodiacPositions.ts.
They'll be imported by NodePositions.


PHASE 2: CREATE THE FOUR CLASSES
---------------------------------

Each class follows the same immutable-with-copyWith pattern as current ZodiacPositions.

2A. FixedStarPositions (new file: fixedStarPositions.ts)
  - Simplest of the four.
  - Depends entirely on: date
  - No changeXYZ methods needed (only date causes change, and date change = full recompute)
  - State: _positions: Map<string, number>
  - Public: getPositions(), getPosition(name)
  - Constructor takes date, optional precomputed positions.

2B. ZodiacSignPositions (new file: zodiacSignPositions.ts)
  - Depends entirely on: date, zodiacMode (renamed from astrologyMode)
  - No partial-recompute changeXYZ needed (both inputs cause full recompute)
  
  USER NOTE: The deduction below is wrong. changeZodiacMode (currently changeAstrologyMode) exists because it only forces recomputation of some of the 4 big objects within ZodiacPositions. The point of splitting is to avoid having to track these complicated dependencies: ZodiacSignPositions does depend entirely on both date and zodiacMode, and both force full recomputation.
    Wait - actually changeZodiacMode exists (was changeAstrologyMode). The date
    triggers full recompute, but zodiacMode can change independently, so:
  - changeZodiacMode(newMode): recomputes sign positions + siderealOffset only
  
  - State:
      _signPositions: Map<Zodiac, number>
      siderealOffset: number | null  (public, as before)
      date: Date
      zodiacMode: ZodiacMode
  - Public methods:
      getSignPositions()
      isRegular(): boolean  (was isZodiacModeRegular)
      getSignAtLongitude(lon): Zodiac  (was _getSymbolAtLongitude)
	  
	  USER NOTE: the deduction below is correct. Turning this idea into a free function in chartAnalysis.ts is preferable. Rewrite these few lines so that the plan is clear, instead of going "this - oh oops, no, maybe that other thing"
      getSignOfNode(lon): Zodiac  -- wait, this takes a Node, it needs NodePositions
        Actually: we refactor this. getSignAtLongitude(lon) is the primitive.
        getSignOfNode was a convenience that did getNodePosition then getSignAtLongitude.
        After the split, callers do: zodiacSignPositions.getSignAtLongitude(nodePositions.get(node))
        Or we keep a convenience as a free function in chartAnalysis.ts.
      
	  getPositionWithinSign(lon): number  (takes raw longitude, not Node)

2C. HouseCuspPositions (new file: houseCuspPositions.ts)
  - Depends entirely on: date, surfacePosition, houseSystem, zodiacSignPositions
  
  USER NOTE: actually the dependence on zodiacSignPositions can be partial, in particular, we make a HouseSystem[], called houseSystemsDependingOnZodiacPositions, which I think would just be whole sign and whole sign aries, and then HouseCuspPositions.changeZodiacSignPositions would just return this if !houseSystemsDependingOnZodiacPositions.includes(this.houseSystem), and otherwise ddo full recomputation. I planned to add this as a TODO but actually it feels quite simple, so please incorporate it into the plan below (and the line above, since the zodiacSignPositions dependency is no longer "entire")
  
  - Depends partially on: housePresweep (trivial - stored config, no recomputation)
  USER NOTE: No recomputation is true, but we do need to use copyWith anyway to preserve immutability.
  
  - Can be null: when surfacePosition is null, or when house system is undefined
    for the given position/time (Placidus/Koch at extreme latitudes).
    So: the producing code returns HouseCuspPositions | null.
  - Eliminates dependency on NodePositions in computeHouseCuspPositions:
    Currently houses.ts:computeHouseCuspPositions takes knownNodes just to extract
    ASC/DSC/MC/IC. Instead, compute these internally from (date, surfacePosition)
    using computeAllSignificantPoints + getTodayEclipticLongitudeFromEQJ (move this
    helper to astronomyUtil.ts or keep in houses.ts as local).
	USER NOTE: Moving to astronomyUtil.ts is preferable. Note it will also be used by NodePositions.
	
    New signature: computeHouseCuspPositions(date, surfacePosition, houseSystem, zodiacSignPositions)
	USER NOTE: Note that this signature does not change when we change the dependency structure as suggested above. This function will NOT get called in the conditions described above, when recomputation is unnecessary.
	
  - changeHouseSystem(newSystem, zodiacSignPositions): recomputes cusps
  - changeHousePresweep(newValue): copyWith, no recomputation
  USER NOTE: boolean for now.
  
  - changeZodiacSignPositions(newZSP): recomputes only if houseSystem is
    ayanamsa-dependant (whole sign systems). Otherwise returns this.
	USER NOTE: Oh wait, this is what I was saying above, you did include it! Okay, so the only change is just making sure that zodiacSignPositions is not an "entire" dependency, i.e. it is not a dependency in the useMemo that App.tsx uses to define houseCuspPositions.
  - State:
      _cuspPositions: number[]
      date, surfacePosition, houseSystem, housePresweep
  - Public methods:
      getCuspPositions(): number[]
      getCuspPosition(i): number
      getHouseOfNode(lon: number): number  (takes longitude, not Node)
        -- presweep logic stays here
      areHouseCuspsWithinHouse(): boolean
        -- returns true if housePresweep is false OR no house is narrower than 5 degrees

2D. NodePositions (new file: nodePositions.ts)
  - The beefiest one. Keeps most helper functions from current zodiacPositions.ts.
  - Depends entirely on: date, surfacePosition
  - Depends partially on: lunarNodeMode, hamburgSchoolMode
  - changeLunarNodeMode(newMode): recomputes lunar nodes + apogee/perigee only
  - changeHamburgSchoolMode(newMode): recomputes hamburg school objects only
  - State:
      _positions: Map<Node, number>
      date, surfacePosition, lunarNodeMode, hamburgSchoolMode
  - Public methods:
      getPositions(): Map<Node, number>
      get(node): number  (was getNodePosition)
      has(node): boolean
      hasSurfacePosition(): boolean
      isAboveHorizon(node): boolean  (was isNodeAboveHorizon)
      isEastern(node): boolean  (was isNodeEastern)
  - Contains/imports all the compute functions:
      computePhysicalNodePositions, computeSmallObjectPositions,
      computeHamburgSchoolObjectPositions, computeAxisAngles,
      computeEquinoxes, computeArabicPartPositions,
      computeAllNodePositions, computeAllNodePositionsWithoutSurfacePosition
  - Imports from astronomyUtil.ts:
      computeLunarNodes, computeLunarApogeePerigee (moved in Phase 1)


PHASE 3: REMOVE computeHouseCuspPositions DEPENDENCY ON NODE POSITIONS
-----------------------------------------------------------------------
USER NOTE: By the way, we haven't yet touched on how we'll be organizing the files, particularly if houses.ts continues being a thing or it will become houseCuspPositions.ts. Just making a note - I assume you'll adress this later in the txt.
In houses.ts, refactor computeHouseCuspPositions:
  - Remove the knownNodes parameter
  - Add date + surfacePosition (already present) to compute axis angles internally
  - Use computeAllSignificantPoints + ecliptic longitude conversion to get ASC/DSC/MC/IC
  - Move getTodayEclipticLongitudeFromEQJ to astronomyUtil.ts (it's a general-purpose
    coordinate conversion) so both nodePositions.ts and houses.ts can use it
  - The space-based house systems already call computeAllSignificantPoints internally,
    so this is actually a deduplication for them
  USER NOTE: Whether this is or isn't a deduplication is rather unclear, since space-based house systems need very different data, even if it comes from the same source. Are you suggesting the dispatcher calls computeAllSignificantPoints itself, turns this into longitude, passes the longitude to who needs it, passes the entire significant point set to the space based house systems, which now take it as a parameter instead of computing it? Or does dispatch only do dispatch, space-based works like it already does, and the ones that need ASC/etc call computeAllSignificantPoints and transform to longitude internally? The latter option seems a bit cleaner to me (dispatch knows a little bit less about the specifics of what data the different methods use internally), but also involves a bit more code. What do you think?

Resulting signature:
  computeHouseCuspPositions(date, surfacePosition, houseSystem, zodiacSignPositions): number[] | null


PHASE 4: DELETE ZodiacPositions, RENAME astrologyUtil.ts
---------------------------------------------------------
- Delete zodiacPositions.ts
- Rename astrologyUtil.ts -> chartAnalysis.ts
- Update all imports

chartAnalysis.ts will contain free functions that operate across position objects:
  - getChartSect(nodePositions) -> Sect
  - isInSect(node, nodePositions) -> boolean | null
  - getChartRuler(nodePositions, zodiacSignPositions, dignityMode) -> Node | null
  - getAngleProximity(node, nodePositions) -> AngleProximityInfo
  - isTrailing(trailingNode, leadingNode, nodePositions) -> boolean
  - getHouseAngularities(nodePositions, houseCuspPositions, houseAngularityMode) -> ...
  - getFixedStarsWithinLongitude(node, nodePositions, fixedStarPositions, maxDist) -> ...
  - getHouseOfNode(node, nodePositions, houseCuspPositions) -> number
    (convenience: pulls lon from nodePositions, calls houseCuspPositions.getHouseOfNode)
  - getSignOfNode(node, nodePositions, zodiacSignPositions) -> Zodiac
    (convenience: pulls lon from nodePositions, calls zodiacSignPositions.getSignAtLongitude)
  - getNodePositionWithinSign(node, nodePositions, zodiacSignPositions) -> number
    (same pattern)
  USER NOTE: probably some others. The intent is to make it so that e.g. NodePositions truly knows nothing other than the node positions, so methods like e.g. isNodeEastern would also become a chartAnalysis.ts function isNodeEastern(node, nodePositions). Oh, and by the way, a VERY important note: this was not the case before, but we want to move into the design philosophy that these functions will error out (instead of just returning null) if the user asks a question that doesn't make sense. E.g. isNodeEastern will error out if nodePositions does not have a surface position, or getHouseOfNode will error out if houseCuspPositions is null. Also an example from below, HouseCuspPositions.create returns an error if selectedCity is null.


PHASE 5: GLOBAL RENAME
------------------------
- "AstrologyMode" -> "ZodiacMode" everywhere (type, enum values, settings store,
  settings UI, variable names). Files affected: astroDefs.ts, settingsDefs.ts,
  settingsStore.ts, settingsMenus.tsx, App.tsx, zodiacSignPositions.ts, houses.ts,
  dignities.ts, any UI that displays mode names.
- "zodiac symbol" / "zodiacSymbol" -> "zodiac sign" / "zodiacSign" everywhere
  (variable names, type names, comments). Notably getZodiacSymbolPositions -> getSignPositions, etc.


PHASE 6: REFACTOR App.tsx
---------------------------
Replace single zodiacPositions state with four:
  const [nodePositions, setNodePositions] = useState(...)
  const [houseCuspPositions, setHouseCuspPositions] = useState<HouseCuspPositions | null>(...)
  const [zodiacSignPositions, setZodiacSignPositions] = useState(...)
  const [fixedStarPositions, setFixedStarPositions] = useState(...)

Full recompute on date/city change:
  useEffect(() => {
    setNodePositions(NodePositions.create(selectedDate, selectedCity, lunarNodeMode, hamburgSchoolMode))
    setZodiacSignPositions(ZodiacSignPositions.create(selectedDate, zodiacMode))
    setFixedStarPositions(FixedStarPositions.create(selectedDate))
    // houseCuspPositions depends on zodiacSignPositions + nodePositions... but we just set them
    // so we need to compute inline:
    const newZSP = ZodiacSignPositions.create(selectedDate, zodiacMode)
    setZodiacSignPositions(newZSP)
    setHouseCuspPositions(selectedCity
      ? HouseCuspPositions.create(selectedDate, selectedCity, houseSystem, newZSP, housePresweep)
      : null)
  }, [selectedCity, selectedDate])

Partial recompute effects:
  useEffect(() => {
    setNodePositions(prev => prev.changeLunarNodeMode(lunarNodeMode))
  }, [lunarNodeMode])

  useEffect(() => {
    setNodePositions(prev => prev.changeHamburgSchoolMode(hamburgSchoolMode))
  }, [hamburgSchoolMode])

  useEffect(() => {
    const newZSP = zodiacSignPositions.changeZodiacMode(zodiacMode)
    setZodiacSignPositions(newZSP)
	USER NOTE: there is no need to have the following logic in App.tsx. We just use setHouseCuspPositions(houseCuspPositions.changeZodiacSignPositions(newZSP)), and the change function handles he logic for whether we need a real update or not.
    // recompute house cusps if ayanamsa-dependant
    if (AyanamsaDependantHouseSystems.includes(houseSystem) && selectedCity) {
      setHouseCuspPositions(HouseCuspPositions.create(
        selectedDate, selectedCity, houseSystem, newZSP, housePresweep))
    }

ZODIAC POSITIONS REFACTOR SPEC
===============================

Goal: Split the ZodiacPositions god object into four focused immutable classes,
each with its own copyWith/changeXYZ pattern, and update all call sites.

NAMING DECISIONS
----------------
- "Zodiac Symbol" -> "Zodiac Sign" (everywhere in the codebase)
- "AstrologyMode" -> "ZodiacMode" (everywhere: type, enum, settings, UI)
- "astrologyUtil.ts" -> "chartAnalysis.ts"
- The four new classes: NodePositions, HouseCuspPositions, ZodiacSignPositions, FixedStarPositions


PHASE 1: EXTRACT HELPER FUNCTIONS
----------------------------------
Move from zodiacPositions.ts to astronomyUtil.ts:
  - computeLunarApogeePerigeeMeeus
  - computeLunarApogeePerigeeExact
  - computeLunarNodesMeeus
  - computeLunarNodesExact
  (Plus their dispatchers computeLunarApogeePerigee, computeLunarNodes)
  USER NOTE: No, their dispatchers stay where they are. The notion of dispatching according to LunarNodeMode we do not consider to be astronomical, it belongs to the object that actually knows that the LunarNodeMode is, i.e. NodePositions.

These are pure astronomy functions with no business being in zodiacPositions.ts.
They'll be imported by NodePositions.


PHASE 2: CREATE THE FOUR CLASSES
---------------------------------

Each class follows the same immutable-with-copyWith pattern as current ZodiacPositions.

2A. FixedStarPositions (new file: fixedStarPositions.ts)
  - Simplest of the four.
  - Depends entirely on: date
  - No changeXYZ methods needed (only date causes change, and date change = full recompute)
  - State: _positions: Map<string, number>
  - Public: getPositions(), getPosition(name)
  - Constructor takes date, optional precomputed positions.

2B. ZodiacSignPositions (new file: zodiacSignPositions.ts)
  - Depends entirely on: date, zodiacMode (renamed from astrologyMode)
  - No partial-recompute changeXYZ needed (both inputs cause full recompute)
  
  USER NOTE: The deduction below is wrong. changeZodiacMode (currently changeAstrologyMode) exists because it only forces recomputation of some of the 4 big objects within ZodiacPositions. The point of splitting is to avoid having to track these complicated dependencies: ZodiacSignPositions does depend entirely on both date and zodiacMode, and both force full recomputation.
    Wait - actually changeZodiacMode exists (was changeAstrologyMode). The date
    triggers full recompute, but zodiacMode can change independently, so:
  - changeZodiacMode(newMode): recomputes sign positions + siderealOffset only
  
  - State:
      _signPositions: Map<Zodiac, number>
      siderealOffset: number | null  (public, as before)
      date: Date
      zodiacMode: ZodiacMode
  - Public methods:
      getSignPositions()
      isRegular(): boolean  (was isZodiacModeRegular)
      getSignAtLongitude(lon): Zodiac  (was _getSymbolAtLongitude)
	  
	  USER NOTE: the deduction below is correct. Turning this idea into a free function in chartAnalysis.ts is preferable. Rewrite these few lines so that the plan is clear, instead of going "this - oh oops, no, maybe that other thing"
      getSignOfNode(lon): Zodiac  -- wait, this takes a Node, it needs NodePositions
        Actually: we refactor this. getSignAtLongitude(lon) is the primitive.
        getSignOfNode was a convenience that did getNodePosition then getSignAtLongitude.
        After the split, callers do: zodiacSignPositions.getSignAtLongitude(nodePositions.get(node))
        Or we keep a convenience as a free function in chartAnalysis.ts.
      
	  getPositionWithinSign(lon): number  (takes raw longitude, not Node)

2C. HouseCuspPositions (new file: houseCuspPositions.ts)
  - Depends entirely on: date, surfacePosition, houseSystem, zodiacSignPositions
  
  USER NOTE: actually the dependence on zodiacSignPositions can be partial, in particular, we make a HouseSystem[], called houseSystemsDependingOnZodiacPositions, which I think would just be whole sign and whole sign aries, and then HouseCuspPositions.changeZodiacSignPositions would just return this if !houseSystemsDependingOnZodiacPositions.includes(this.houseSystem), and otherwise ddo full recomputation. I planned to add this as a TODO but actually it feels quite simple, so please incorporate it into the plan below (and the line above, since the zodiacSignPositions dependency is no longer "entire")
  
  - Depends partially on: housePresweep (trivial - stored config, no recomputation)
  USER NOTE: No recomputation is true, but we do need to use copyWith anyway to preserve immutability.
  
  - Can be null: when surfacePosition is null, or when house system is undefined
    for the given position/time (Placidus/Koch at extreme latitudes).
    So: the producing code returns HouseCuspPositions | null.
  - Eliminates dependency on NodePositions in computeHouseCuspPositions:
    Currently houses.ts:computeHouseCuspPositions takes knownNodes just to extract
    ASC/DSC/MC/IC. Instead, compute these internally from (date, surfacePosition)
    using computeAllSignificantPoints + getTodayEclipticLongitudeFromEQJ (move this
    helper to astronomyUtil.ts or keep in houses.ts as local).
	USER NOTE: Moving to astronomyUtil.ts is preferable. Note it will also be used by NodePositions.
	
    New signature: computeHouseCuspPositions(date, surfacePosition, houseSystem, zodiacSignPositions)
	USER NOTE: Note that this signature does not change when we change the dependency structure as suggested above. This function will NOT get called in the conditions described above, when recomputation is unnecessary.
	
  - changeHouseSystem(newSystem, zodiacSignPositions): recomputes cusps
  - changeHousePresweep(newValue): copyWith, no recomputation
  USER NOTE: boolean for now.
  
  - changeZodiacSignPositions(newZSP): recomputes only if houseSystem is
    ayanamsa-dependant (whole sign systems). Otherwise returns this.
	USER NOTE: Oh wait, this is what I was saying above, you did include it! Okay, so the only change is just making sure that zodiacSignPositions is not an "entire" dependency, i.e. it is not a dependency in the useMemo that App.tsx uses to define houseCuspPositions.
  - State:
      _cuspPositions: number[]
      date, surfacePosition, houseSystem, housePresweep
  - Public methods:
      getCuspPositions(): number[]
      getCuspPosition(i): number
      getHouseOfNode(lon: number): number  (takes longitude, not Node)
        -- presweep logic stays here
      areHouseCuspsWithinHouse(): boolean
        -- returns true if housePresweep is false OR no house is narrower than 5 degrees

2D. NodePositions (new file: nodePositions.ts)
  - The beefiest one. Keeps most helper functions from current zodiacPositions.ts.
  - Depends entirely on: date, surfacePosition
  - Depends partially on: lunarNodeMode, hamburgSchoolMode
  - changeLunarNodeMode(newMode): recomputes lunar nodes + apogee/perigee only
  - changeHamburgSchoolMode(newMode): recomputes hamburg school objects only
  - State:
      _positions: Map<Node, number>
      date, surfacePosition, lunarNodeMode, hamburgSchoolMode
  - Public methods:
      getPositions(): Map<Node, number>
      get(node): number  (was getNodePosition)
      has(node): boolean
      hasSurfacePosition(): boolean
      isAboveHorizon(node): boolean  (was isNodeAboveHorizon)
      isEastern(node): boolean  (was isNodeEastern)
  - Contains/imports all the compute functions:
      computePhysicalNodePositions, computeSmallObjectPositions,
      computeHamburgSchoolObjectPositions, computeAxisAngles,
      computeEquinoxes, computeArabicPartPositions,
      computeAllNodePositions, computeAllNodePositionsWithoutSurfacePosition
  - Imports from astronomyUtil.ts:
      computeLunarNodes, computeLunarApogeePerigee (moved in Phase 1)


PHASE 3: REMOVE computeHouseCuspPositions DEPENDENCY ON NODE POSITIONS
-----------------------------------------------------------------------
USER NOTE: By the way, we haven't yet touched on how we'll be organizing the files, particularly if houses.ts continues being a thing or it will become houseCuspPositions.ts. Just making a note - I assume you'll adress this later in the txt.
In houses.ts, refactor computeHouseCuspPositions:
  - Remove the knownNodes parameter
  - Add date + surfacePosition (already present) to compute axis angles internally
  - Use computeAllSignificantPoints + ecliptic longitude conversion to get ASC/DSC/MC/IC
  - Move getTodayEclipticLongitudeFromEQJ to astronomyUtil.ts (it's a general-purpose
    coordinate conversion) so both nodePositions.ts and houses.ts can use it
  - The space-based house systems already call computeAllSignificantPoints internally,
    so this is actually a deduplication for them
  USER NOTE: Whether this is or isn't a deduplication is rather unclear, since space-based house systems need very different data, even if it comes from the same source. Are you suggesting the dispatcher calls computeAllSignificantPoints itself, turns this into longitude, passes the longitude to who needs it, passes the entire significant point set to the space based house systems, which now take it as a parameter instead of computing it? Or does dispatch only do dispatch, space-based works like it already does, and the ones that need ASC/etc call computeAllSignificantPoints and transform to longitude internally? The latter option seems a bit cleaner to me (dispatch knows a little bit less about the specifics of what data the different methods use internally), but also involves a bit more code. What do you think?

Resulting signature:
  computeHouseCuspPositions(date, surfacePosition, houseSystem, zodiacSignPositions): number[] | null


PHASE 4: DELETE ZodiacPositions, RENAME astrologyUtil.ts
---------------------------------------------------------
- Delete zodiacPositions.ts
- Rename astrologyUtil.ts -> chartAnalysis.ts
- Update all imports

chartAnalysis.ts will contain free functions that operate across position objects:
  - getChartSect(nodePositions) -> Sect
  - isInSect(node, nodePositions) -> boolean | null
  - getChartRuler(nodePositions, zodiacSignPositions, dignityMode) -> Node | null
  - getAngleProximity(node, nodePositions) -> AngleProximityInfo
  - isTrailing(trailingNode, leadingNode, nodePositions) -> boolean
  - getHouseAngularities(nodePositions, houseCuspPositions, houseAngularityMode) -> ...
  - getFixedStarsWithinLongitude(node, nodePositions, fixedStarPositions, maxDist) -> ...
  - getHouseOfNode(node, nodePositions, houseCuspPositions) -> number
    (convenience: pulls lon from nodePositions, calls houseCuspPositions.getHouseOfNode)
  - getSignOfNode(node, nodePositions, zodiacSignPositions) -> Zodiac
    (convenience: pulls lon from nodePositions, calls zodiacSignPositions.getSignAtLongitude)
  - getNodePositionWithinSign(node, nodePositions, zodiacSignPositions) -> number
    (same pattern)
  USER NOTE: probably some others. The intent is to make it so that e.g. NodePositions truly knows nothing other than the node positions, so methods like e.g. isNodeEastern would also become a chartAnalysis.ts function isNodeEastern(node, nodePositions). Oh, and by the way, a VERY important note: this was not the case before, but we want to move into the design philosophy that these functions will error out (instead of just returning null) if the user asks a question that doesn't make sense. E.g. isNodeEastern will error out if nodePositions does not have a surface position, or getHouseOfNode will error out if houseCuspPositions is null. Also an example from below, HouseCuspPositions.create returns an error if selectedCity is null.


PHASE 5: GLOBAL RENAME
------------------------
- "AstrologyMode" -> "ZodiacMode" everywhere (type, enum values, settings store,
  settings UI, variable names). Files affected: astroDefs.ts, settingsDefs.ts,
  settingsStore.ts, settingsMenus.tsx, App.tsx, zodiacSignPositions.ts, houses.ts,
  dignities.ts, any UI that displays mode names.
- "zodiac symbol" / "zodiacSymbol" -> "zodiac sign" / "zodiacSign" everywhere
  (variable names, type names, comments). Notably getZodiacSymbolPositions -> getSignPositions, etc.


PHASE 6: REFACTOR App.tsx
---------------------------
Replace single zodiacPositions state with four:
  const [nodePositions, setNodePositions] = useState(...)
  const [houseCuspPositions, setHouseCuspPositions] = useState<HouseCuspPositions | null>(...)
  const [zodiacSignPositions, setZodiacSignPositions] = useState(...)
  const [fixedStarPositions, setFixedStarPositions] = useState(...)

Full recompute on date/city change:
  useEffect(() => {
    setNodePositions(NodePositions.create(selectedDate, selectedCity, lunarNodeMode, hamburgSchoolMode))
    setZodiacSignPositions(ZodiacSignPositions.create(selectedDate, zodiacMode))
    setFixedStarPositions(FixedStarPositions.create(selectedDate))
    // houseCuspPositions depends on zodiacSignPositions + nodePositions... but we just set them
    // so we need to compute inline:
    const newZSP = ZodiacSignPositions.create(selectedDate, zodiacMode)
    setZodiacSignPositions(newZSP)
    setHouseCuspPositions(selectedCity
      ? HouseCuspPositions.create(selectedDate, selectedCity, houseSystem, newZSP, housePresweep)
      : null)
  }, [selectedCity, selectedDate])

Partial recompute effects:
  useEffect(() => {
    setNodePositions(prev => prev.changeLunarNodeMode(lunarNodeMode))
  }, [lunarNodeMode])

  useEffect(() => {
    setNodePositions(prev => prev.changeHamburgSchoolMode(hamburgSchoolMode))
  }, [hamburgSchoolMode])

  useEffect(() => {
    const newZSP = zodiacSignPositions.changeZodiacMode(zodiacMode)
    setZodiacSignPositions(newZSP)
	USER NOTE: there is no need to have the following logic in App.tsx. We just use setHouseCuspPositions(houseCuspPositions.changeZodiacSignPositions(newZSP)), and the change function handles he logic for whether we need a real update or not.
    // recompute house cusps if ayanamsa-dependant
    if (AyanamsaDependantHouseSystems.includes(houseSystem) && selectedCity) {
      setHouseCuspPositions(HouseCuspPositions.create(
        selectedDate, selectedCity, houseSystem, newZSP, housePresweep))
    }
  }, [zodiacMode])

  useEffect(() => {
	USER NOTE: avoid these sorts of checks, do selectedCity !== null if that's what you mean (null is the default absent value here, yes)
    setHouseCuspPositions(selectedCity
      ? HouseCuspPositions.create(selectedDate, selectedCity, houseSystem, zodiacSignPositions, housePresweep)
      : null)
  }, [houseSystem])

  useEffect(() => {
    setHouseCuspPositions(prev => prev?.changeHousePresweep(housePresweep) ?? null)
  }, [housePresweep])
	
	date: Date;
	surfacePosition: SurfacePosition | null;
	lunarNodeMode: LunarNodeMode;
	houseSystem: HouseSystem;

PHASE 7: REFACTOR ALL CONSUMER COMPONENTS
-------------------------------------------
Walk through every component/file that currently takes zodiacPositions and replace

ZODIAC POSITIONS REFACTOR SPEC
===============================

Goal: Split the ZodiacPositions god object into four focused immutable classes,
and update all call sites.

NAMING DECISIONS
----------------
- "Zodiac Symbol" -> "Zodiac Sign" (everywhere in the codebase)
- "AstrologyMode" -> "ZodiacMode" (everywhere: type, enum, settings, UI)
- "astrologyUtil.ts" -> "chartAnalysis.ts"
- "houses.ts" -> "houseCuspPositions.ts" (computation logic stays in-file)
- The four new classes: NodePositions, HouseCuspPositions, ZodiacSignPositions, FixedStarPositions

DESIGN PHILOSOPHY
-----------------
- All four classes are immutable. Config values (date, surfacePosition, lunarNodeMode,
  etc.) are private (prefixed with _). Each class exposes only what external code needs.
- chartAnalysis.ts functions throw errors on nonsensical inputs rather than returning
  null. E.g. isNodeEastern throws if nodePositions has no surface position;
  getHouseOfNode throws if houseCuspPositions is null. HouseCuspPositions.create
  throws if surfacePosition is null (caller must check before calling).


PHASE 1: EXTRACT HELPER FUNCTIONS
----------------------------------
Move from zodiacPositions.ts to astronomyUtil.ts:
  - computeLunarApogeePerigeeMeeus
  - computeLunarApogeePerigeeExact
  - computeLunarNodesMeeus
  - computeLunarNodesExact
Also move getTodayEclipticLongitudeFromEQJ to astronomyUtil.ts (general-purpose
coordinate conversion, used by both nodePositions.ts and houseCuspPositions.ts).

The dispatchers (computeLunarApogeePerigee, computeLunarNodes) stay with
NodePositions — dispatching by LunarNodeMode is a domain decision, not astronomy.

---------------------------------

  - Simplest of the four.

  - Public: getPositions(), getPosition(name)
  - Constructor takes date, optional precomputed positions.

2B. ZodiacSignPositions (new file: zodiacSignPositions.ts)
  - Depends entirely on: date, zodiacMode
  - No changeXYZ methods (both inputs cause full recompute — the whole point
    of the split is that we no longer need to track cross-object dependencies)
  - Private state: _date, _zodiacMode, _signPositions: Map<Zodiac, number>
  - Public state: siderealOffset: number | null
  - Public methods:
      getSignPositions(): Map<Zodiac, number>
      isRegular(): boolean  (was isZodiacModeRegular)
      getSignAtLongitude(lon): Zodiac  (was _getSymbolAtLongitude)
      getPositionWithinSign(lon): number  (takes raw longitude, not Node)
  - Note: getSignOfNode does NOT live here (it needs NodePositions). It becomes

  - changeZodiacSignPositions(newZSP): recomputes cusps only if houseSystem is in

      getCuspPositions(): number[]
      getCuspPosition(i): number
      getHouseOfNode(lon: number): number  (takes longitude, not Node; presweep logic here)

ZODIAC POSITIONS REFACTOR SPEC
===============================

Goal: Split the ZodiacPositions god object into four focused immutable classes,
and update all call sites.

NAMING DECISIONS
----------------
- "Zodiac Symbol" -> "Zodiac Sign" (everywhere in the codebase)
- "AstrologyMode" -> "ZodiacMode" (everywhere: type, enum, settings, UI)
- "astrologyUtil.ts" -> "chartAnalysis.ts"
- "houses.ts" -> "houseCuspPositions.ts" (computation logic stays in-file)
- The four new classes: NodePositions, HouseCuspPositions, ZodiacSignPositions, FixedStarPositions

DESIGN PHILOSOPHY
-----------------
- All four classes are immutable. Config values (date, surfacePosition, lunarNodeMode,
  etc.) are private (prefixed with _). Each class exposes only what external code needs.
- chartAnalysis.ts functions throw errors on nonsensical inputs rather than returning
  null. E.g. isNodeEastern throws if nodePositions has no surface position;
  getHouseOfNode throws if houseCuspPositions is null. HouseCuspPositions.create
  throws if surfacePosition is null (caller must check before calling).


PHASE 1: EXTRACT HELPER FUNCTIONS
----------------------------------
Move from zodiacPositions.ts to astronomyUtil.ts:
  - computeLunarApogeePerigeeMeeus
  - computeLunarApogeePerigeeExact
  - computeLunarNodesMeeus
  - computeLunarNodesExact
Also move getTodayEclipticLongitudeFromEQJ to astronomyUtil.ts (general-purpose
coordinate conversion, used by both nodePositions.ts and houseCuspPositions.ts).

The dispatchers (computeLunarApogeePerigee, computeLunarNodes) stay with
NodePositions — dispatching by LunarNodeMode is a domain decision, not astronomy.


PHASE 2: CREATE THE FOUR CLASSES
---------------------------------

2A. FixedStarPositions (new file: fixedStarPositions.ts)
  - Simplest of the four.
  - Depends entirely on: date
  - No changeXYZ methods (date change = full recompute)
  - Private state: _date, _positions: Map<string, number>
  - Public: getPositions(), getPosition(name)
  - Constructor takes date, optional precomputed positions.

2B. ZodiacSignPositions (new file: zodiacSignPositions.ts)
  - Depends entirely on: date, zodiacMode
  - No changeXYZ methods (both inputs cause full recompute — the whole point
    of the split is that we no longer need to track cross-object dependencies)
  - Private state: _date, _zodiacMode, _signPositions: Map<Zodiac, number>
  - Public state: siderealOffset: number | null
  - Public methods:
      getSignPositions(): Map<Zodiac, number>
      isRegular(): boolean  (was isZodiacModeRegular)
      getSignAtLongitude(lon): Zodiac  (was _getSymbolAtLongitude)
      getPositionWithinSign(lon): number  (takes raw longitude, not Node)
  - Note: getSignOfNode does NOT live here (it needs NodePositions). It becomes
    a free function getSignOfNode(node, nodePositions, zodiacSignPositions) in
    chartAnalysis.ts.
  - Computation functions (private/local to file):
      computeSiderealOffset, computeZodiacSignPositionsFromSiderealOffset,
      computeZodiacSignPositionsForIrregularMode

2C. HouseCuspPositions (new file: houseCuspPositions.ts)
  - houses.ts is renamed to houseCuspPositions.ts. All house computation logic
    stays in-file — nobody else needs to know how houses are computed.
  - Depends entirely on: date, surfacePosition, houseSystem
  - Depends partially on: zodiacSignPositions (only matters for house systems in
    AyanamsaDependantHouseSystems, which already exists in current houses.ts)

    system is undefined for the position/time (Placidus/Koch at extreme latitudes).

    is responsible for checking.
  - computeHouseCuspPositions no longer depends on NodePositions (see Phase 3).
  - changeHouseSystem(newSystem, zodiacSignPositions): full cusp recompute
  - changeHousePresweep(newValue: boolean): copyWith, no cusp recomputation
  - changeZodiacSignPositions(newZSP): recomputes cusps only if houseSystem is in
    AyanamsaDependantHouseSystems. Otherwise returns this.
  - Private state: _date, _surfacePosition, _houseSystem, _housePresweep,
    _cuspPositions: number[]
  - Public methods:
      getCuspPositions(): number[]
      getCuspPosition(i): number
      getHouseOfNode(lon: number): number  (takes longitude, not Node; presweep logic here)
      areHouseCuspsWithinHouse(): boolean
        -- returns true if housePresweep is false OR no house is narrower than 5 degrees

  - The beefiest one. Keeps most helper functions from current zodiacPositions.ts.

      getPositions(): Map<Node, number>
      get(node): number  (was getNodePosition)

      hasSurfacePosition(): boolean
  - Note: isAboveHorizon and isEastern do NOT live here. NodePositions truly just

ZODIAC POSITIONS REFACTOR SPEC
===============================

Goal: Split the ZodiacPositions god object into four focused immutable classes,
each with its own copyWith/changeXYZ pattern, and update all call sites.

NAMING DECISIONS
----------------
- "Zodiac Symbol" -> "Zodiac Sign" (everywhere in the codebase)
- "AstrologyMode" -> "ZodiacMode" (everywhere: type, enum, settings, UI)
- "astrologyUtil.ts" -> "chartAnalysis.ts"
- The four new classes: NodePositions, HouseCuspPositions, ZodiacSignPositions, FixedStarPositions


PHASE 1: EXTRACT HELPER FUNCTIONS
----------------------------------
Move from zodiacPositions.ts to astronomyUtil.ts:
  - computeLunarApogeePerigeeMeeus
  - computeLunarApogeePerigeeExact
  - computeLunarNodesMeeus
  - computeLunarNodesExact
  (Plus their dispatchers computeLunarApogeePerigee, computeLunarNodes)
  USER NOTE: No, their dispatchers stay where they are. The notion of dispatching according to LunarNodeMode we do not consider to be astronomical, it belongs to the object that actually knows that the LunarNodeMode is, i.e. NodePositions.

These are pure astronomy functions with no business being in zodiacPositions.ts.
They'll be imported by NodePositions.


PHASE 2: CREATE THE FOUR CLASSES
---------------------------------

Each class follows the same immutable-with-copyWith pattern as current ZodiacPositions.

2A. FixedStarPositions (new file: fixedStarPositions.ts)
  - Simplest of the four.
  - Depends entirely on: date
  - No changeXYZ methods needed (only date causes change, and date change = full recompute)
  - State: _positions: Map<string, number>
  - Public: getPositions(), getPosition(name)
  - Constructor takes date, optional precomputed positions.

2B. ZodiacSignPositions (new file: zodiacSignPositions.ts)
  - Depends entirely on: date, zodiacMode (renamed from astrologyMode)
  - No partial-recompute changeXYZ needed (both inputs cause full recompute)
  
  USER NOTE: The deduction below is wrong. changeZodiacMode (currently changeAstrologyMode) exists because it only forces recomputation of some of the 4 big objects within ZodiacPositions. The point of splitting is to avoid having to track these complicated dependencies: ZodiacSignPositions does depend entirely on both date and zodiacMode, and both force full recomputation.
    Wait - actually changeZodiacMode exists (was changeAstrologyMode). The date
    triggers full recompute, but zodiacMode can change independently, so:
  - changeZodiacMode(newMode): recomputes sign positions + siderealOffset only
  
  - State:
      _signPositions: Map<Zodiac, number>
      siderealOffset: number | null  (public, as before)
      date: Date
      zodiacMode: ZodiacMode
  - Public methods:
      getSignPositions()
      isRegular(): boolean  (was isZodiacModeRegular)
      getSignAtLongitude(lon): Zodiac  (was _getSymbolAtLongitude)
	  
	  USER NOTE: the deduction below is correct. Turning this idea into a free function in chartAnalysis.ts is preferable. Rewrite these few lines so that the plan is clear, instead of going "this - oh oops, no, maybe that other thing"
      getSignOfNode(lon): Zodiac  -- wait, this takes a Node, it needs NodePositions
        Actually: we refactor this. getSignAtLongitude(lon) is the primitive.
        getSignOfNode was a convenience that did getNodePosition then getSignAtLongitude.
        After the split, callers do: zodiacSignPositions.getSignAtLongitude(nodePositions.get(node))
        Or we keep a convenience as a free function in chartAnalysis.ts.
      
	  getPositionWithinSign(lon): number  (takes raw longitude, not Node)

2C. HouseCuspPositions (new file: houseCuspPositions.ts)
  - Depends entirely on: date, surfacePosition, houseSystem, zodiacSignPositions
  
  USER NOTE: actually the dependence on zodiacSignPositions can be partial, in particular, we make a HouseSystem[], called houseSystemsDependingOnZodiacPositions, which I think would just be whole sign and whole sign aries, and then HouseCuspPositions.changeZodiacSignPositions would just return this if !houseSystemsDependingOnZodiacPositions.includes(this.houseSystem), and otherwise ddo full recomputation. I planned to add this as a TODO but actually it feels quite simple, so please incorporate it into the plan below (and the line above, since the zodiacSignPositions dependency is no longer "entire")
  
  - Depends partially on: housePresweep (trivial - stored config, no recomputation)
  USER NOTE: No recomputation is true, but we do need to use copyWith anyway to preserve immutability.
  
  - Can be null: when surfacePosition is null, or when house system is undefined
    for the given position/time (Placidus/Koch at extreme latitudes).
    So: the producing code returns HouseCuspPositions | null.
  - Eliminates dependency on NodePositions in computeHouseCuspPositions:
    Currently houses.ts:computeHouseCuspPositions takes knownNodes just to extract
    ASC/DSC/MC/IC. Instead, compute these internally from (date, surfacePosition)
    using computeAllSignificantPoints + getTodayEclipticLongitudeFromEQJ (move this
    helper to astronomyUtil.ts or keep in houses.ts as local).
	USER NOTE: Moving to astronomyUtil.ts is preferable. Note it will also be used by NodePositions.
	
    New signature: computeHouseCuspPositions(date, surfacePosition, houseSystem, zodiacSignPositions)
	USER NOTE: Note that this signature does not change when we change the dependency structure as suggested above. This function will NOT get called in the conditions described above, when recomputation is unnecessary.
	
  - changeHouseSystem(newSystem, zodiacSignPositions): recomputes cusps
  - changeHousePresweep(newValue): copyWith, no recomputation
  USER NOTE: boolean for now.
  
  - changeZodiacSignPositions(newZSP): recomputes only if houseSystem is
    ayanamsa-dependant (whole sign systems). Otherwise returns this.
	USER NOTE: Oh wait, this is what I was saying above, you did include it! Okay, so the only change is just making sure that zodiacSignPositions is not an "entire" dependency, i.e. it is not a dependency in the useMemo that App.tsx uses to define houseCuspPositions.
  - State:
      _cuspPositions: number[]
      date, surfacePosition, houseSystem, housePresweep
  - Public methods:
      getCuspPositions(): number[]
      getCuspPosition(i): number
      getHouseOfNode(lon: number): number  (takes longitude, not Node)
        -- presweep logic stays here
      areHouseCuspsWithinHouse(): boolean
        -- returns true if housePresweep is false OR no house is narrower than 5 degrees

2D. NodePositions (new file: nodePositions.ts)
  - The beefiest one. Keeps most helper functions from current zodiacPositions.ts.
  - Depends entirely on: date, surfacePosition
  - Depends partially on: lunarNodeMode, hamburgSchoolMode
  - changeLunarNodeMode(newMode): recomputes lunar nodes + apogee/perigee only
  - changeHamburgSchoolMode(newMode): recomputes hamburg school objects only
  - State:
      _positions: Map<Node, number>
      date, surfacePosition, lunarNodeMode, hamburgSchoolMode
  - Public methods:
      getPositions(): Map<Node, number>
      get(node): number  (was getNodePosition)
      has(node): boolean
      hasSurfacePosition(): boolean
      isAboveHorizon(node): boolean  (was isNodeAboveHorizon)
      isEastern(node): boolean  (was isNodeEastern)
  - Contains/imports all the compute functions:
      computePhysicalNodePositions, computeSmallObjectPositions,
      computeHamburgSchoolObjectPositions, computeAxisAngles,
      computeEquinoxes, computeArabicPartPositions,
      computeAllNodePositions, computeAllNodePositionsWithoutSurfacePosition
  - Imports from astronomyUtil.ts:
      computeLunarNodes, computeLunarApogeePerigee (moved in Phase 1)


PHASE 3: REMOVE computeHouseCuspPositions DEPENDENCY ON NODE POSITIONS
-----------------------------------------------------------------------
USER NOTE: By the way, we haven't yet touched on how we'll be organizing the files, particularly if houses.ts continues being a thing or it will become houseCuspPositions.ts. Just making a note - I assume you'll adress this later in the txt.
In houses.ts, refactor computeHouseCuspPositions:
  - Remove the knownNodes parameter
  - Add date + surfacePosition (already present) to compute axis angles internally
  - Use computeAllSignificantPoints + ecliptic longitude conversion to get ASC/DSC/MC/IC
  - Move getTodayEclipticLongitudeFromEQJ to astronomyUtil.ts (it's a general-purpose
    coordinate conversion) so both nodePositions.ts and houses.ts can use it
  - The space-based house systems already call computeAllSignificantPoints internally,
    so this is actually a deduplication for them
  USER NOTE: Whether this is or isn't a deduplication is rather unclear, since space-based house systems need very different data, even if it comes from the same source. Are you suggesting the dispatcher calls computeAllSignificantPoints itself, turns this into longitude, passes the longitude to who needs it, passes the entire significant point set to the space based house systems, which now take it as a parameter instead of computing it? Or does dispatch only do dispatch, space-based works like it already does, and the ones that need ASC/etc call computeAllSignificantPoints and transform to longitude internally? The latter option seems a bit cleaner to me (dispatch knows a little bit less about the specifics of what data the different methods use internally), but also involves a bit more code. What do you think?

Resulting signature:
  computeHouseCuspPositions(date, surfacePosition, houseSystem, zodiacSignPositions): number[] | null


PHASE 4: DELETE ZodiacPositions, RENAME astrologyUtil.ts
---------------------------------------------------------
- Delete zodiacPositions.ts
- Rename astrologyUtil.ts -> chartAnalysis.ts
- Update all imports

chartAnalysis.ts will contain free functions that operate across position objects:
  - getChartSect(nodePositions) -> Sect
  - isInSect(node, nodePositions) -> boolean | null
  - getChartRuler(nodePositions, zodiacSignPositions, dignityMode) -> Node | null
  - getAngleProximity(node, nodePositions) -> AngleProximityInfo
  - isTrailing(trailingNode, leadingNode, nodePositions) -> boolean
  - getHouseAngularities(nodePositions, houseCuspPositions, houseAngularityMode) -> ...
  - getFixedStarsWithinLongitude(node, nodePositions, fixedStarPositions, maxDist) -> ...
  - getHouseOfNode(node, nodePositions, houseCuspPositions) -> number
    (convenience: pulls lon from nodePositions, calls houseCuspPositions.getHouseOfNode)
  - getSignOfNode(node, nodePositions, zodiacSignPositions) -> Zodiac
    (convenience: pulls lon from nodePositions, calls zodiacSignPositions.getSignAtLongitude)
  - getNodePositionWithinSign(node, nodePositions, zodiacSignPositions) -> number
    (same pattern)
  USER NOTE: probably some others. The intent is to make it so that e.g. NodePositions truly knows nothing other than the node positions, so methods like e.g. isNodeEastern would also become a chartAnalysis.ts function isNodeEastern(node, nodePositions). Oh, and by the way, a VERY important note: this was not the case before, but we want to move into the design philosophy that these functions will error out (instead of just returning null) if the user asks a question that doesn't make sense. E.g. isNodeEastern will error out if nodePositions does not have a surface position, or getHouseOfNode will error out if houseCuspPositions is null. Also an example from below, HouseCuspPositions.create returns an error if selectedCity is null.


PHASE 5: GLOBAL RENAME
------------------------
- "AstrologyMode" -> "ZodiacMode" everywhere (type, enum values, settings store,
  settings UI, variable names). Files affected: astroDefs.ts, settingsDefs.ts,
  settingsStore.ts, settingsMenus.tsx, App.tsx, zodiacSignPositions.ts, houses.ts,
  dignities.ts, any UI that displays mode names.
- "zodiac symbol" / "zodiacSymbol" -> "zodiac sign" / "zodiacSign" everywhere
  (variable names, type names, comments). Notably getZodiacSymbolPositions -> getSignPositions, etc.


PHASE 6: REFACTOR App.tsx
---------------------------
Replace single zodiacPositions state with four:
  const [nodePositions, setNodePositions] = useState(...)
  const [houseCuspPositions, setHouseCuspPositions] = useState<HouseCuspPositions | null>(...)
  const [zodiacSignPositions, setZodiacSignPositions] = useState(...)
  const [fixedStarPositions, setFixedStarPositions] = useState(...)

Full recompute on date/city change:
  useEffect(() => {
    setNodePositions(NodePositions.create(selectedDate, selectedCity, lunarNodeMode, hamburgSchoolMode))
    setZodiacSignPositions(ZodiacSignPositions.create(selectedDate, zodiacMode))
    setFixedStarPositions(FixedStarPositions.create(selectedDate))
    // houseCuspPositions depends on zodiacSignPositions + nodePositions... but we just set them

PHASE 6: REFACTOR App.tsx
---------------------------
Replace single zodiacPositions state with four:
  const [nodePositions, setNodePositions] = useState(...)
  const [houseCuspPositions, setHouseCuspPositions] = useState<HouseCuspPositions | null>(...)
  const [zodiacSignPositions, setZodiacSignPositions] = useState(...)
  const [fixedStarPositions, setFixedStarPositions] = useState(...)

Full recompute on date/city change:
  useEffect(() => {
    const newNodePositions = NodePositions.create(selectedDate, selectedCity, lunarNodeMode, hamburgSchoolMode)
    const newZSP = ZodiacSignPositions.create(selectedDate, zodiacMode)
    setNodePositions(newNodePositions)
    setZodiacSignPositions(newZSP)
    setFixedStarPositions(FixedStarPositions.create(selectedDate))
    setHouseCuspPositions(selectedCity !== null
      ? HouseCuspPositions.create(selectedDate, selectedCity, houseSystem, newZSP, housePresweep)
      : null)
  }, [selectedCity, selectedDate])

Partial recompute effects:
  useEffect(() => {
    setNodePositions(prev => prev.changeLunarNodeMode(lunarNodeMode))
  }, [lunarNodeMode])

  useEffect(() => {
    setNodePositions(prev => prev.changeHamburgSchoolMode(hamburgSchoolMode))
  }, [hamburgSchoolMode])

  useEffect(() => {
    const newZSP = ZodiacSignPositions.create(selectedDate, zodiacMode)
    setZodiacSignPositions(newZSP)
    setHouseCuspPositions(prev => prev?.changeZodiacSignPositions(newZSP) ?? null)
  }, [zodiacMode])

  useEffect(() => {
    setHouseCuspPositions(selectedCity !== null
      ? HouseCuspPositions.create(selectedDate, selectedCity, houseSystem, zodiacSignPositions, housePresweep)
      : null)
  }, [houseSystem])

  useEffect(() => {
    setHouseCuspPositions(prev => prev?.changeHousePresweep(housePresweep) ?? null)
  }, [housePresweep])

content.text:
The issue is a timing gap: `setSelectedCity` triggers a render where `selectedCity` is non-null but `houseCuspPositions` is still null (the useEffect that computes it hasn't run yet). So for one frame the condition fires.

A couple of approaches:

**Option 1 — Set houseCuspPositions eagerly in the city selection handler.** In the `onSelect` callback where you call `setSelectedCity(city)`, also immediately call `setHouseCuspPositions(HouseCuspPositions.create(...))` right there. React batches both state updates in the same event handler, so the intermediate state is never rendered. The useEffect will still fire afterward and redundantly re-set it, which is harmless.

**Option 2 — Track a separate `houseSystemFailed` boolean.** Instead of inferring failure from `houseCuspPositions === null`, have the computation logic explicitly set a `houseSystemFailed` state to `true` when `HouseCuspPositions.create` returns null *despite* having a valid city. The popup condition becomes just `houseSystemFailed`. This way null means "not yet computed or no city" and never triggers the popup on its own.

Option 1 is simpler and more direct — it eliminates the flash without adding new state. Option 2 is more robust conceptually (the popup's visibility is based on an explicit signal rather than inferred from two states being out of sync), but adds a piece of state that must be kept consistent everywhere houseCuspPositions is set.

Fix: cast `zodiac` in the map callback:

```ts
[zodiac as Zodiac, addPrecession(date, lon)]
```

content.text:
You're right, I was wrong about that. When lunarNodeMode changes, `changeLunarNodeMode` on both n1 and n2 only recomputes the lunar node positions — no full `create` call. My `useMemo` approach would force a full `NodePositions.create` for n2 on every change, even partial ones, which defeats the whole purpose of the `changeXYZ` pattern.

So the real tradeoff is:

Your concern is not an issue. useState initializer functions (the `() => ...` lazy initializer form) run **synchronously** during the first render, in declaration order. By the time line 106 executes, line 105 has already completed and `nodePositions` holds the fully constructed value.

The lazy initializer isn't deferred or async — its whole purpose is just to avoid re-running the computation on subsequent re-renders (unlike passing the value directly, which would call `NodePositions.create(...)` every render and then throw the result away). But on the first render, it runs immediately and synchronously, top to bottom, just like any other code.

So if I have some const [value, setValue] = useState(someExpensiveComputation());, you're telling me that someExpensiveComputation runs on EVERY re-render even if the value doesn't get used anywhere? Like, does js not have sufficiently smart evaluation to realize it doesn't need to compute that? Certainly I was 100% under the impression that something like false || someExpensiveComputation() would NOT evaluate someExpensiveComputation. Am I wrong? content.text:
You're right about `false || someExpensiveComputation()` — that's short-circuit evaluation and JS absolutely does skip the right side. That's a language-level guarantee.

But `useState(someExpensiveComputation())` is different. There's no short-circuiting here. It's just a normal function call:

```ts
const result = someExpensiveComputation(); // runs first
useState(result);                          // then this receives the value
```

JS evaluates arguments before passing them to functions. `useState` has no way to prevent that — by the time it receives the value, the computation already happened. `useState` just internally ignores the argument after the first render (it returns the stored state instead), but the argument was still computed.

That's exactly why the `() =>` lazy initializer form exists:

```ts
useState(() => someExpensiveComputation());
```

Here you're passing a *function* to `useState`, which is cheap. `useState` then decides whether to *call* that function — it only calls it on the first render and skips it on subsequent renders.

So to summarize: not a JS quirk, not a React quirk, just standard function call semantics. Arguments are evaluated before the function can do anything about them.
